title: Hierarchical authorization contracts and permission derivation
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary:
Design and specification for RBAC v2 role model centered on explicit authorization contracts, deterministic permission derivation, and a resource hierarchy that enables tenant-scoped least privilege. This ticket scopes the core data model, evaluation rules, audit event contract, and SSO/SAML attribute mapping required for first-phase implementation on the platform-API and console.

Goals:
- Define an expressive but deterministic role model supporting role-sets, ephemeral grants, and resource-pattern scopes (tenant, project, region, model-instance).
- Produce a permissions derivation algorithm that is order-independent and explainable for audit and UI needs.
- Ensure audit logs include resolution context (effective roles, inferred permissions, evaluation path) to satisfy compliance.
- Define SAML/SSO attribute mappings and default role bindings for IdP-initiated provisioning and just-in-time grants.
- Specify admin controls (delegated admins, emergency unlocks, immutable system roles) and safe migration path from RBAC v1.

Design highlights:
1) Resource hierarchy and scope model:
- Canonical levels: Organization > Tenant > Project > Model > Deployment/Pool > Route.
- Each resource has a canonical identifier and optional pattern form (e.g., tenant:acme, project:acme/*, model:acme/model-*) to support wildcard scopes.
- Scopes are a pair of (resource-pattern, scope-kind) where scope-kind is one of {read, write, manage, admin, audit}.

2) Roles and role-sets:
- Atomic roles are small permission bundles (e.g., model.read, model.infer, model.manage).
- Role-sets are unordered collections of atomic roles. A principal can have multiple bindings; effective permissions are the union of derived permissions after conflict rules.
- System roles (system.admin, system.audit-reader) are immutable and live at org scope.

3) Permission derivation rules (deterministic and explainable):
- Binding form: {principal, role, scope-pattern, grant-meta}. Grant-meta includes source (manual, sso-mapped, api-token), creation_time, expiry(optional), and delegation flag.
- Evaluation algorithm: compute all matching bindings for the requested resource by matching scope-patterns; expand role-sets to permissions; apply expiry and delegation filters; union permissions; then apply deny-overrides where explicit deny bindings exist. No first-match semantics.
- Explainability: evaluation returns an ordered list of contributing bindings and the minimal set of roles that led to each permission. This data becomes part of audit events and the console Explanation pane.

4) Deny semantics and overrides:
- Introduce explicit deny bindings with higher priority than grants. Deny bindings are always resource-scoped and cannot be wildcarded to org-level.
- No implicit denies except default-no-access.

5) SSO/SAML and provisioning mapping:
- Two flows supported: IdP provisioning (SCIM/enterprise sync) and SAML JIT role mapping.
- Attribute map example: saml:groups -> potential role-set names; saml:entitlements -> scope-limited grants (JSON string with {role,scope-pattern}).
- For JIT grants, we persist a synthetic binding with source=sso-mapped and ttl=24h by default; admins can configure longer sync overrides via console policies.
- We record IdP assertion id, mapping rule id, and user principal in grant-meta for traceability.

6) Audit logging contract and events:
- Every authorization evaluation emits an auth_evaluation event containing: request_id, principal_id, resource_id, requested_action, effective_permissions (list), contributing_bindings (list of binding ids), timestamp, evaluation_duration_ms.
- All binding changes (create/update/delete, including SSO syncs) emit binding_change events including before/after snapshots and actor.
- Admin actions (emergency-grant, revoke, role-create) emit admin_audit events with justification text required for emergency actions.
- Logs are JSON-lines and must include correlated_trace_id to tie into console traces and request logs.

7) Admin controls and emergency flows:
- Delegated admin role model: allow tenant-scoped admin roles that can only manage resources within their scope.
- Emergency unlock: time-bound 'break-glass' grants require multi-person approval (2 approvers) and produce an immutable admin_audit entry; system auto-revokes after expiry.
- Prefer policy-driven delegation over ad-hoc owner grants.

8) Migration strategy from RBAC v1:
- Compatibility pass: import v1 roles into role-sets with metadata linking to original binding id.
- Dual-eval mode: for a rollout window, evaluate both v1 and v2 and emit comparison metrics to the console. We will default to v2 after 6 weeks or when parity metrics show <0.1% divergence.

Sample permission matrix (excerpt):
Resource Level | Atomic Permission   | Typical Role Name
Organization    | org.view            | org.viewer
Tenant          | tenant.manage        | tenant.admin
Project         | project.deploy       | project.deployer
Model           | model.infer          | model.consumer
Model           | model.upload         | model.publisher
Deployment      | deployment.scale     | infra.operator
Audit           | audit.read           | audit.reader

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We chose union-based derivation (no first-match) to make evaluation explainable and stable under rule reordering. Cost: slightly heavier evaluation path; mitigated by a cache of compiled binding sets per-resource that invalidates on binding changes.
- Deny-overrides simplifies security posture; downside is complexity in migration where previous implicit allowances existed. Migration tooling will flag potential denies and require manual review.
- SAML attribute-free-form entitlements support gives flexibility but requires validation; plan to ship a safe-mode sandbox for IdP admins to test mappings before live.

- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Authorization+Contracts
- Design sketches: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-rbac-v2-design
- Prototype service PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/2142
- Console mockups: https://figma.com/file/xyz/RBAC-v2-Console

Open questions / TODOs:
- Default TTL for JIT SSO grants (ops, compliance input needed).
- How to represent resource-pattern complexity in query planner for fast matching; we have a strawman trie-based matcher but need benchmarks.
- Exact schema for contributing_bindings in auth_evaluation events (ids vs full snapshots).

Acceptance criteria:
- API: create/list/update/delete binding endpoints for role-sets, supports scope-patterns and deny flag.
- Auth evaluator: deterministic, returns explainability payload, and emits auth_evaluation events.
- Console: role-explain view showing contributing bindings and effective permissions for a given principal/resource.
- Migration: dual-eval mode enabled and parity dashboard available.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement core data model and evaluator in auth-service behind feature flag (2 sprints).
2) Wire audit events to existing logging infra and add console UI for explanation (1 sprint).
3) SSO mapping and JIT flows with TTL defaults and sandbox (1 sprint).
4) Migration tooling and final cutover (2 sprints).
